summary.title: Deep Learning and Medical Image Analysis with Keras
summary.one_liner: You learn how to build a Keras/ResNet classifier that detects malaria in blood smear cell images, splitting the NIH cell-image dataset into train, validation and test sets.
keywords: how to detect malaria with deep learning
takeaways: The NIH malaria dataset has 27,588 blood smear images in two classes, Parasitized and Uninfected, with 13,794 per class.
Splitting the data into training, validation and testing sets is done with a short script that shuffles image paths and copies files into per-class folders.
The approach reuses a ResNet implementation from the author's book to reach roughly 97% accuracy with a smaller, more efficient model than the six-model NIH approach.
Training uses a polynomial learning rate decay over 50 epochs with an initial learning rate of 1e-1 and batch size 32.
summary.summary: The tutorial explains how deep learning can help with malaria screening, motivating a single, compact model over the six pre-trained networks used in NIH's 2018 work. It walks through the NIH cell-image dataset and the project layout, including a config.py file that sets dataset paths and split ratios (80% train, with 10% of that held out for validation). A build_dataset.py script shuffles the images and copies them into training, validation and testing folders. The post then starts train_model.py, which uses Keras with a ResNet model, a polynomial learning rate schedule and a matplotlib plot. The page text ends before the training results, so the final accuracy is only stated as roughly 97% in the body.
